sources.title: 2025 Concise Clinical Guidance: an ACC expert consensus statement on the evaluation and management of cardiogenic shock (ACC; Sinha SS, Morrow DA, Kapur NK, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol, doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2025.02.018)
ESICM guidelines on circulatory shock and hemodynamic monitoring 2025 (ESICM; Monnet X, et al. Intensive Care Med)
SCAI SHOCK Stages Classification Expert Consensus Update: A Review and Incorporation of Validation Studies (SCAI; Naidu SS, et al.)

q_cs.text: Hypoperfusion with a likely cardiac cause (with or without low BP)?

q_mech.text: Echo: mechanical cause? (tamponade, acute severe valve lesion, septal or papillary muscle rupture)

q_rhythm.text: Is an arrhythmia driving the shock?

q_ecg.text: 12-lead ECG: ST elevation or acute ischaemia?

q_bp.text: Is the patient hypotensive (MAP below 60-65 mmHg)?

q_response.text: Response to vasoactive therapy so far?

e_not_cs.title: Cardiogenic cause not confirmed
actions: Go to the pathway: Shock: initial recognition and type.
Echo and 12-lead ECG to clarify.
cautions: Normotensive cardiogenic shock exists and carries high mortality (ACC 2025).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_mech.title: Mechanical cause of shock
actions: Tamponade: urgent drainage.
Acute valve lesion or rupture: urgent cardiology and cardiac surgery review.
Call the regional shock centre early about transfer.
cautions: Specific management of mechanical complications was not covered in the sources reviewed: these steps are standard practice, follow specialist advice.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_brady.title: Bradycardia-driven shock
actions: Go to the pathway: Bradycardia (adult, with a pulse).
12-lead ECG now if not already done (ACC 2025: every patient with suspected cardiogenic shock).
ST elevation or acute ischaemia: treat as shock with acute MI as well; early revascularisation, activate the cath lab or arrange urgent transfer to a PCI centre (ACC 2025).
A chronotrope (e.g. isoproterenol) may be trialled in bradycardia-induced shock (ACC 2025).
Prepare pacing.
cautions: Check for drug causes and hyperkalaemia.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_tachy.title: Tachyarrhythmia-driven shock
actions: Go to the pathway: Tachycardia with a pulse (adult), unstable branch.
12-lead ECG now if not already done (ACC 2025: every patient with suspected cardiogenic shock).
ST elevation or acute ischaemia: treat as shock with acute MI as well; early revascularisation, activate the cath lab or arrange urgent transfer to a PCI centre (ACC 2025).
Synchronised cardioversion is the usual first step when a tachyarrhythmia causes shock.
cautions: Cardioversion energies: see the pathway Tachycardia with a pulse (adult).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_ami.title: Shock with acute MI
actions: Early revascularisation: activate cath lab or arrange urgent transfer to a PCI centre.
Early revascularisation is the only intervention with proven mortality benefit in MI shock (ACC 2025).
Support MAP above 60-65 mmHg with norepinephrine.
Contact the regional shock centre as soon as cardiogenic shock is confirmed (ACC 2025 advises early contact).
cautions: Routine temporary mechanical support for all patients is discouraged; a microaxial flow pump may be considered in selected STEMI shock with LV-dominant failure (specialist centre decision).
IABP did not improve mortality in MI shock (IABP-SHOCK II).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_inodilator.title: Normotensive cardiogenic shock
actions: Consider an inodilator, especially if systemic vascular resistance is high.
Dobutamine 2-10 mcg/kg/min (weight-based; ACC 2025 range).
Or milrinone 0.125-0.5 mcg/kg/min (weight-based; ACC 2025 range).
Treat congestion with IV loop diuretic.
Serial lactate, urine output and echo; consider invasive haemodynamics early.
cautions: Dobutamine and milrinone are inodilators (ACC 2025): watch for falling BP on the arterial line.
Milrinone: long half-life, renally cleared; care in renal impairment.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_start_ne.title: Hypotensive cardiogenic shock: start support
actions: Norepinephrine is a reasonable first choice; ACC 2025 range 0.05-1 mcg/kg/min (weight-based).
MAP target above 60-65 mmHg.
Arterial line (ESICM 2025).
Add an inotrope if hypoperfusion persists once MAP is adequate.
Stage the shock (SCAI SHOCK stages) and contact the shock team or regional centre.
cautions: Do not use phenylephrine as the sole first-line agent (reflex bradycardia, lower cardiac output).
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_refractory.title: Refractory cardiogenic shock
actions: Urgent shock-team discussion: cardiology, cardiac surgery, intensivist.
Discuss transfer to a Level 1 shock centre if refractory to initial drug therapy.
Consider invasive haemodynamics (PA catheter) to guide escalation.
Temporary mechanical support decision by the specialist centre.
Consider early palliative care input where appropriate.
cautions: Ask early: any absolute contraindication to escalation (e.g. DNR, terminal illness)?
Assess whether the patient is stable enough to transfer.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_diuretic.title: Left-sided congestion
actions: IV loop diuretic; add a thiazide if response is poor (ACC 2025).
Refractory congestion: renal replacement therapy for ultrafiltration.
Respiratory support for pulmonary oedema as needed.
Continue to reassess perfusion; keep MAP above 60-65 mmHg.
cautions: Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_rv.title: RV-dominant shock
actions: Look for the cause: RV infarction, pulmonary embolism, acute pulmonary hypertension, ventilation effects.
Urgent cardiology input.
Invasive haemodynamics can help define the pattern.
cautions: The ACC 2025 guidance gives no specific RV-shock treatment steps: management needs specialist and local-protocol input.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_continue.title: Improving: continue and reassess
actions: Reassess often, especially in the first 24-72 hours.
Labs every 2-4 hours early on, then every 6-8 hours when stable (ACC 2025).
Daily echo or POCUS.
Wean vasoactive drugs to the lowest effective dose.
cautions: Most patients change shock stage within 24 hours: be ready to escalate.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_add_inotrope.title: Add an inotrope
actions: MAP above 60-65 mmHg but still hypoperfused: add an inotrope.
Dobutamine 2-10 mcg/kg/min (weight-based; ACC 2025 range).
Or milrinone 0.125-0.5 mcg/kg/min (weight-based; ACC 2025 range).
Recheck lactate, urine output and echo after each change; consider invasive haemodynamics.
If still hypoperfused: re-enter and choose 'norepinephrine plus inotrope'.
cautions: Dobutamine and milrinone are inodilators (ACC 2025): watch for falling BP on the arterial line.
Milrinone: long half-life, renally cleared; use with care in renal impairment.
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_map_low.title: On norepinephrine, MAP still low
actions: Uptitrate norepinephrine within the ACC 2025 range, 0.05-1 mcg/kg/min (weight-based), towards MAP above 60-65 mmHg.
Urgent shock-team discussion: cardiology, cardiac surgery, intensivist.
Refractory to initial drug therapy: consult and consider transfer to a Level 1 shock centre, including discussion of mechanical circulatory support (ACC 2025).
Recheck for a mechanical cause, arrhythmia or ischaemia (repeat echo and ECG).
Do not start an inodilator alone while MAP is below target (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).
cautions: Dobutamine and milrinone are inodilators (ACC 2025) and can lower BP further.
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.
